summary: This lecture is part 26 of a detailed commentary on Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Ibn al-Qayyim al-Jawziyyah, presented by Sheikh Ali Mashhour. The session focuses on Salat al-Duha (the forenoon prayer), discussing its status in Islamic jurisprudence, the Prophet's practice regarding it, and the wisdom of not overextending oneself in acts of worship that might discourage others. The lecture then transitions to cover Sujud al-Shukur (prostration of gratitude) and Sujud al-Tilawah (prostration of recitation), explaining their rulings, conditions, and the etiquette surrounding these practices according to Islamic law.
